questions.q: Which number system uses only the digits 0 and 1?
questions.explain: Binary is base 2, so it only uses 0 and 1. Computers use it because transistors have two states: on and off.

questions.q: What is the denary value of the binary number 1010?
Why do programmers often use hexadecimal instead of binary?
options: It uses less memory in the computer
It is shorter and easier for humans to read and less error-prone
questions.explain: Hexadecimal is only a shorthand for binary: one hex digit stands for four bits. The computer still stores binary.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: 1 byte = 8 bits. A nibble is 4 bits.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary number for denary 25?
questions.explain: 25 = 16 + 8 + 1, so the bits for 16, 8 and 1 are on: 00011001.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal value of the binary number 11111010?
questions.explain: Split into nibbles: 1111 = F and 1010 = A, giving FA.

questions.q: A logical left shift of 2 places is applied to 00001011. What is the result, and what is the effect?
questions.explain: Each left shift doubles the value. Two shifts multiply by 4: 11 x 4 = 44 = 00101100.

questions.q: What happens when 11001000 and 01100100 are added in an 8-bit register?
options: The answer is 00101100 with no error
The answer is 100101100 and is stored correctly
An overflow error occurs because the result needs 9 bits
questions.explain: 200 + 100 = 300, which is bigger than the largest 8-bit value (255). The result cannot fit, so overflow occurs.

questions.q: An image is 8 pixels wide and 8 pixels high with a colour depth of 4 bits. What is the file size?
questions.explain: 8 x 8 = 64 pixels x 4 bits = 256 bits. 256 / 8 = 32 bytes.

questions.q: Which statement about lossless compression is correct?
options: The original file can be rebuilt exactly
It always gives a smaller file than lossy
It is only used for sound files
questions.explain: Lossless compression keeps all the data, so the original can be restored exactly. Lossy permanently removes data.

questions.q: Which change makes a recorded sound file larger AND the recording more accurate?
options: Lower sampling rate and lower bit depth
Higher sampling rate and higher bit depth
Higher sampling rate and lower bit depth
questions.explain: More samples per second and more bits per sample capture the wave more accurately, but need more storage.

questions.q: What is -5 in 8-bit two's complement?
What is the main advantage of Unicode over ASCII?
options: It uses fewer bits per character
It can represent characters from many more languages
It is only used for numbers
questions.explain: ASCII has 128 (or 256 extended) characters. Unicode has a far larger character set covering most languages and symbols.

questions.q: What is the binary result of 1 + 1?
questions.explain: 1 + 1 = 2 in denary, which is 10 in binary (0 carry 1).

questions.q: Which part of a data packet holds the destination address and packet number?
questions.explain: The header holds the destination address, the originator's address and the packet number. The payload is the data itself.

questions.q: In packet switching, what can happen to the packets of one message?
options: They all take the same route in order
They can take different routes and arrive in any order
They are sent as a single block
questions.explain: Each packet is routed independently and the receiving device puts them back in order using the packet numbers.

questions.q: Which method sends data one bit at a time down a single wire?
questions.explain: Serial sends one bit after another along one wire. Parallel sends several bits at once along several wires.

questions.q: Why is parallel transmission unsuitable for long distances?
options: It is always slower than serial
Bits can arrive out of sync (skewed) and interfere with each other
questions.explain: Over long cables the bits on the separate wires arrive at slightly different times (skew) and cause crosstalk.

questions.q: A walkie-talkie lets two people talk, but only one at a time. Which transmission mode is this?
questions.explain: Half-duplex: both directions, but not at the same time. Full-duplex is both at once. Simplex is one direction only.

questions.q: Using EVEN parity, what parity bit should be added to 1011001?
questions.explain: 1011001 has four 1s, which is already even, so the parity bit is 0.

questions.q: How does Automatic Repeat Request (ARQ) deal with errors?
options: It corrects the error without resending
It uses acknowledgements and timeouts to request resending of data
questions.explain: The receiver sends a positive or negative acknowledgement. If none arrives before the timeout, the sender resends the packet.

questions.q: Which check sends data back to the sender so it can be compared with the original?
questions.explain: An echo check returns the received data to the sender. If it differs from what was sent, an error occurred. It cannot tell whether the error happened on the way there or back.

questions.q: Which statement about asymmetric encryption is correct?
options: The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
Only a public key is used
A public key encrypts and a different private key decrypts
questions.explain: Asymmetric encryption uses a key pair. Anyone can use the public key to encrypt, but only the owner's private key can decrypt.

questions.q: Why is USB described as a serial interface?
options: It transmits data one bit at a time
It is slower than all other methods
It sends data in only one direction
questions.explain: USB (Universal Serial Bus) sends data bit by bit down a wire, which avoids skew and works well over short and medium distances.

questions.q: What is the name of encrypted data that cannot be read without a key? (one word)
questions.explain: Plaintext goes through an encryption algorithm to become ciphertext.

questions.q: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explain: The Central Processing Unit processes instructions and data.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
questions.explain: An instruction is fetched from memory, decoded by the control unit, then executed.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.explain: The Program Counter holds the address of the next instruction and is incremented after each fetch.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU carries out calculations and logical comparisons?
questions.explain: The ALU performs arithmetic (add, subtract) and logic (AND, OR, NOT, comparisons). The control unit manages the process.

questions.q: Which bus carries the memory location that is going to be read from or written to?
questions.explain: The address bus carries addresses one way (from CPU to memory). The data bus carries data both ways. The control bus carries control signals.

questions.q: Which change would normally improve the performance of a CPU?
options: More cores and a larger cache
questions.explain: More cores allow more instructions to be processed at once. A larger cache keeps more frequently used data close to the CPU. A higher clock speed also helps.

questions.q: Which statement about ROM is correct?
options: It loses its contents when switched off
It is non-volatile and often stores the start-up instructions
It is used to store the user's open documents
questions.explain: ROM is non-volatile. It keeps its contents without power and holds the bootstrap. RAM is volatile.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of an SSD compared with a magnetic hard disk drive?
options: It has no moving parts so it is faster and more durable
It can be written to an unlimited number of times
It uses a laser to read data
questions.explain: An SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts. It is quieter, faster and more shock resistant, but costs more per GB.

questions.q: When is virtual memory used?
options: When the RAM is full, so part of the secondary storage is used as extra RAM
When the computer is switched off
questions.explain: Virtual memory moves pages of data from RAM to secondary storage when RAM is full. It is much slower than real RAM.

questions.q: Which statement about a MAC address is correct?
options: It is assigned by the router and changes each time
It is a unique hardware address of a network interface card, set by the manufacturer
It is the same as the IP address
It is used only on the internet
questions.explain: A MAC address identifies the network interface card. An IP address is assigned by the network and can change.

questions.q: A two-input AND gate gives an output of 1. What must the inputs be?
questions.explain: AND outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.

questions.q: For which pair of inputs does an XOR gate output 1?
questions.explain: XOR outputs 1 only when the inputs are different.

questions.q: Memory that loses its contents when the power is switched off is described as what? (volatile / non-volatile)
questions.explain: RAM is volatile: it loses its contents when power is lost. ROM and secondary storage are non-volatile.

questions.q: Which of these is system software?
questions.explain: System software runs and manages the computer (operating system, utilities, drivers). The others are application software.

questions.q: Which of these is a job of the operating system?
questions.explain: The operating system manages memory, files, devices, multitasking, security and the user interface.

questions.q: What is an interrupt?
options: A virus that stops the computer
A signal to the processor that something needs attention immediately
A fault in the hardware that cannot be fixed
questions.explain: An interrupt is a signal from a device or program asking the CPU to pause its current task and deal with something more urgent.

questions.q: Which statement about high-level languages is correct?
options: They depend on the specific processor
They are easier for humans to read and write, and need translating
questions.explain: High-level languages are close to English and portable, but must be compiled or interpreted into machine code.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates the whole program at once, an interpreter translates and runs it line by line
A compiler only works for assembly code
An interpreter produces an executable file, a compiler does not
questions.explain: A compiler produces an executable of the whole program and reports all errors at the end. An interpreter executes one line at a time and stops at the first error.

questions.q: Which translator converts assembly language into machine code?
questions.explain: An assembler translates assembly language mnemonics into machine code.

questions.q: Which of these is a typical feature of an IDE?
options: Breakpoints, a debugger and syntax highlighting
questions.explain: An Integrated Development Environment helps programmers with a code editor, a translator, a debugger, breakpoints, a variable watch and error diagnostics.

questions.q: Which utility software finds and removes malware?
questions.explain: Anti-virus software scans files and removes or quarantines malware.

questions.q: What does disk defragmentation do on a magnetic hard disk?
options: Rearranges file parts so they are stored together in contiguous sectors
questions.explain: Files get split across the disk over time. Defragmentation puts the pieces next to each other, so the read head moves less.

questions.q: Why might a programmer choose a low-level language?
options: To make the program portable to all computers
To make the program easy to read
To control hardware directly and make efficient use of memory
To avoid the need for any translator
questions.explain: Low-level languages give direct control of the hardware and memory. They are used for device drivers and embedded systems, but are harder to write and not portable.

questions.q: What does OS stand for? (two words)
questions.explain: OS = Operating System.

questions.q: What is the difference between the internet and the World Wide Web?
options: The internet is the network infrastructure, the WWW is the collection of web pages accessed through it
The WWW is the hardware, the internet is the software
questions.explain: The internet is the global network of networks. The World Wide Web is a service that runs on it and consists of websites and pages.

questions.q: What does a web browser do?
options: Converts domain names to IP addresses
Stores web pages on the server
Renders HTML and displays web pages
questions.explain: A browser requests web pages and displays them by rendering the HTML. The DNS converts domain names to IP addresses.

questions.q: What does the Domain Name System (DNS) do?
options: Translates a domain name into an IP address
questions.explain: DNS servers hold a database that maps domain names (e.g. www.example.com) to IP addresses.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of HTTPS over HTTP?
questions.explain: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS to encrypt data between the browser and the server, so it cannot easily be read if intercepted.

questions.q: Which of these is a use of session cookies?
options: Storing a user's items in an online shopping basket during a visit
Keeping a user's login for a year
Infecting the computer with a virus
questions.explain: Session cookies exist only while the browser is open, e.g. a shopping basket. Persistent cookies stay after the browser is closed.

questions.q: An email pretending to be from a bank asks you to click a link and enter your password. What is this?
questions.explain: Phishing uses fake emails to trick users into giving away personal details. Pharming redirects users to a fake website without them clicking a link in an email.

questions.q: What is the aim of a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack?
options: To flood a server with requests so it cannot serve real users
questions.explain: Many computers (often a botnet) send huge numbers of requests until the server is overwhelmed and legitimate users are denied service.

questions.q: Which malware locks a user's files and demands payment to unlock them?
questions.explain: Ransomware encrypts the user's data and demands a ransom for the key.

questions.q: What does a firewall do?
options: Monitors incoming and outgoing traffic and blocks anything that breaks the rules
questions.explain: A firewall examines network traffic against a set of criteria and blocks unauthorised access.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a digital certificate on a website?
options: To prove the website is genuine and provide its public key
questions.explain: A digital certificate, issued by a certificate authority, shows that the website's owner is verified and holds the public key used for SSL/TLS.

questions.q: Which of these describes a blockchain?
options: A backup stored on one central server
A digital ledger of transactions where each block is linked to the previous one
questions.explain: Each block holds transactions and the hash of the previous block, so past records are hard to alter. It underpins cryptocurrencies.

questions.q: In an "IP address", what does the P stand for? (one word)
questions.explain: IP = Internet Protocol.

questions.q: In an automated system, which component converts a physical quantity such as temperature into data?
questions.explain: Sensors input data from the environment. The microprocessor processes it and actuators make something happen.

questions.q: What is the job of an actuator?
options: To carry out a physical action such as opening a valve or turning a motor
questions.explain: Actuators are the output devices of control systems. They convert signals from the microprocessor into movement.

questions.q: A greenhouse heater switches on when the temperature drops below a set value and off when it reaches it. Which feature makes this automatic control possible?
options: Feedback from the sensor to the microprocessor
questions.explain: The sensor's output (feedback) lets the microprocessor compare readings with the target and adjust the actuator.

questions.q: Which of these is a typical characteristic of a robot?
options: It is controlled by a computer program and has mechanical parts
questions.explain: A robot has a mechanical structure, electrical components such as sensors and motors, and is programmable.

questions.q: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
options: A computer that has been connected to the internet
A computer that copies files faster
A computer system that can perform tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as learning and decision making
questions.explain: AI systems use rules and data to reason, learn, and make decisions, for example speech recognition and image recognition.

questions.q: How does machine learning differ from a normal programmed system?
options: It improves its own performance from data without being explicitly reprogrammed for each case
It always gives the same output
questions.explain: Machine learning trains a model on data so it can adapt and improve its accuracy, rather than following only fixed hand-written rules.

questions.q: Which part of an expert system applies the rules in the rule base to the knowledge base to reach a conclusion?
questions.explain: Expert system parts: knowledge base (facts), rule base (IF-THEN rules), inference engine (reasoning), user interface and explanation system.

questions.q: Which is a possible advantage of driverless (autonomous) vehicles?
options: They remove all risk of accidents
They can reduce accidents caused by human error
questions.explain: Autonomous vehicles use sensors and AI and do not get tired or distracted. Disadvantages include cost, hacking risk and ethical decisions in unavoidable accidents.

questions.q: What is the difference between virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR)?
options: VR places digital content over the real world, AR replaces it
VR replaces the real world with a computer-generated one, AR overlays digital content on the real world
AR needs a headset but VR does not
questions.explain: VR immerses the user in a simulated world, usually with a headset. AR adds digital objects to a live view of the real world, e.g. on a phone camera.

questions.q: Which is a possible negative impact of using robots in manufacturing?
options: Loss of jobs for manual workers
Robots can work 24 hours a day
questions.explain: Robots increase productivity and consistency but can replace human workers, leading to unemployment and a need for retraining.

questions.q: Name the input device in a control system that measures things like light, temperature or pressure. (one word)
questions.explain: A sensor measures a physical property and sends the data to the microprocessor.
